Direct answer: Suspension height affects magnetic separator performance because the air gap between the magnet and the material reduces the magnetic force that reaches tramp iron. On African mining, quarry, cement and aggregate conveyors, a separator mounted too high may fail to lift buried or small ferrous pieces even when the magnet itself is correctly built.

This guide is for buyers comparing overband magnetic separators, suspended permanent magnets and suspended electromagnetic separators for crusher protection. It explains how installation height, burden depth, belt speed and tramp iron size work together, and what data Cowin Magnet needs before recommending a model.

The goal is not to choose the strongest magnet on paper. The goal is to match magnetic reach to the real conveyor condition, with enough clearance for safe material flow and enough access for maintenance.

Key Takeaways

  • Suspension height is the distance from the magnet face to the top of the conveyed material, and it directly affects magnetic reach.
  • Burden depth matters together with suspension height because tramp iron may sit below the surface of the material bed.
  • Overband magnetic separators should be installed as low as safely practical while allowing lump clearance and stable belt operation.
  • High belt speed reduces capture time, so high-speed conveyors need closer review of magnet position and magnetic force.
  • Permanent and electromagnetic separators can both be suitable, but the final choice depends on height, burden depth and duty severity.
  • A quotation should include conveyor drawings, photos and measured installation height instead of only belt width.

Use Case: Crusher Protection on African Conveyors

In mining and quarrying plants, tramp metal can enter the material stream from drill steel, loader teeth, bolts, screen media, crusher wear parts, rail fragments and maintenance debris. If ferrous metal reaches a jaw crusher, cone crusher, impact crusher, mill feed point or screen, it can cause damage, belt cuts or unplanned shutdowns.

A suspended magnet or overband magnetic separator is usually installed above a conveyor before the crusher or transfer point. In South Africa, Zambia, Zimbabwe, DRC, Ghana, Nigeria and Kenya, these conveyors often handle mixed lump sizes, abrasive ore, wet aggregate, coal, limestone or recycled material under tough outdoor conditions.

The magnet must reach through the air gap and the material burden. If the magnet is mounted too high because of a walkway, chute, dust hood or structural beam, performance can drop. This is why suspension height should be measured during selection, not guessed after purchase.

Recommended Equipment Types

A self-cleaning overband magnetic separator is commonly recommended when tramp metal appears regularly and the conveyor runs continuously. It uses a cleaning belt to carry captured ferrous metal away from the conveyor and discharge it to one side. This helps reduce manual cleaning and keeps the protection point active during operation.

A suspended permanent magnetic separator can be suitable when tramp metal is occasional, the burden depth is moderate and the site can clean the magnet safely during planned stops. It is often reviewed for simpler crusher protection duties where power availability is limited or where a manual-cleaning solution is acceptable.

A suspended electromagnetic conveyor belt separator may be reviewed when the burden is deeper, the required suspension height is higher, or the plant needs adjustable magnetic force. It requires electrical power and control equipment, so buyers should consider power stability, cable routing, cooling, inspection access and maintenance capability.

What Suspension Height Means in Practice

Suspension height is often misunderstood. Buyers may measure from the magnet frame to the conveyor belt, but the more useful number is the working distance from the magnet face to the top of the material burden. The magnet must first cross this air gap before it can influence ferrous metal in the material stream.

For crusher protection, the practical question is simple: where is the tramp iron located when it passes under the magnet? If it lies on top of the material, capture is easier. If it is buried in ore, aggregate, coal or limestone, the magnet must reach through more material. A deep burden plus a large air gap is one of the most common reasons for weak separation results.

Plant layout can make this harder. Transfer chutes, dust covers, belt mistracking allowance, large lump clearance and existing steelwork may force the separator higher than ideal. These constraints should be reviewed before quotation so the equipment is selected for the real position.

Key Selection Parameters

Belt width defines the required coverage across the conveyor, but it does not define magnetic performance by itself. A 1,000 mm belt carrying a shallow layer of aggregate is different from a 1,000 mm belt carrying deep copper ore or wet coal. The material profile on the belt must be considered.

Burden depth is critical. Measure the normal and maximum material depth at the proposed installation point. Also note whether the material is loaded centrally or off-centre. Off-centre loading may require position adjustment or a wider magnetic coverage area.

Belt speed affects capture time. On a fast conveyor, tramp iron spends less time in the magnetic field. Larger ferrous pieces are usually easier to attract than small or deeply buried pieces, but shape and orientation also matter. Moisture can increase material cling and make buried tramp metal harder to recover.

The working environment should also be provided. Outdoor African plants may face dust, rain, heat, vibration and limited maintenance windows. These conditions influence guarding, cleaning method, motor selection, control placement and inspection access.

Common Mistakes with Installation Height

The first mistake is treating suspension height as a minor installation detail. It is a selection parameter. If the supplier designs for a lower height but the site mounts the separator higher, the final result may not match expectations.

The second mistake is ignoring the top of burden. A conveyor may look easy from a side photo, but if the material bed is deep at full load, the effective magnetic distance increases. Always provide burden depth under normal and peak capacity conditions.

The third mistake is installing the magnet above turbulent material immediately after a transfer point without checking material stability. If the burden is bouncing, spreading or surging, capture can become inconsistent. A stable belt section before the crusher is often better when the layout allows it.

The fourth mistake is forgetting the discharge path. Self-cleaning overband magnets need room to discharge captured metal safely. The discharge side must not be blocked by walkways, cable trays, handrails or structure.

Installation and Maintenance Notes

Install the separator where it can intercept tramp metal before critical equipment. For many crusher protection systems, this means before the crusher feed point, before a screen, or before a transfer chute that leads to sensitive downstream equipment. The structure must support the separator weight and allow safe adjustment of height and angle.

For cross-belt overband installation, check that captured metal can move away from the main conveyor and drop into a bin or chute. For inline installation, review whether discharge direction and tramp iron trajectory are practical. Guarding, lockout procedures and access platforms should be included in the layout discussion.

Maintenance teams should inspect the cleaning belt, bearings, motor, guards, suspension points, discharge chute and collected tramp metal. For electromagnetic models, include the control cabinet, cables and cooling system in the inspection plan. Dust buildup around motors and moving parts should not be ignored in quarry, cement and coal applications.

When the Product Is Suitable

An overband or suspended magnetic separator is suitable when the site needs to remove ferrous tramp metal from a conveyor before crushers, screens, feeders, mills or transfer equipment. It is especially relevant for gold mines, copper mines, coal conveyors, limestone handling, aggregate plants, cement raw material handling and recycling lines.

It is also suitable when the buyer can provide enough installation clearance, a safe support frame and a practical discharge or cleaning method. If tramp iron is expected frequently, a self-cleaning model should usually be reviewed first.

When the Product Is Not Suitable

A standard conveyor magnet is not suitable for removing most non-ferrous metals such as aluminium, copper or brass. If the buyer needs non-ferrous detection or recovery, a metal detector or eddy current separator should be considered separately.

The product may also be unsuitable as a simple drop-in solution if the separator must be mounted too high, if burden depth is excessive, or if there is no safe discharge area. In those cases, the plant may need to change the installation point, reduce burden depth, improve material loading or combine separation with detection.

Information Needed Before Quotation

Before requesting a quote, send measured operating data from the conveyor. Do not rely only on a belt width, a photo or a desired magnet size. Cowin Magnet needs to understand the distance the magnetic field must work across, the material it must reach through and the size of tramp iron the plant wants to remove.

Useful supporting files include conveyor general arrangement drawings, photos from both sides of the belt, close-up photos of the proposed support area, and a sketch showing available height. If the plant has already experienced crusher damage or belt cuts, describe the typical ferrous object size and where it entered the process.

FAQ

How does suspension height affect magnetic separator performance?

Suspension height affects performance because magnetic force reduces as the working distance increases. If an overband or suspended magnet is mounted too high above the material, it may not attract small, buried or fast-moving ferrous pieces reliably. The important measurement is the distance from the magnet face to the top of the material burden, plus the burden depth that tramp iron may be buried under.

What is the best installation height for an overband magnet?

There is no universal best height. The correct height depends on belt width, material burden depth, belt speed, particle size, tramp iron size and available clearance. In general, the magnet should be installed as low as safely practical while allowing material flow, lump clearance and stable conveyor operation. Cowin Magnet should review measured site data before recommending a model and installation position.

Can a stronger magnet solve a high suspension height problem?

A stronger magnet can sometimes help, but it is not always the best or only solution. If the separator is mounted very high or the burden is very deep, the plant may need to change the installation point, reduce burden depth, improve loading or consider an electromagnetic separator. Selection should compare magnetic reach, layout limits, cleaning method, power and maintenance access together.

Should the magnet be installed before or after the crusher?

For crusher protection, the magnet is normally installed before the crusher so ferrous tramp metal can be removed before it reaches the crushing chamber. The best point is usually a stable conveyor section with enough clearance and a safe discharge path. If the only available space is after the crusher, it may still help downstream equipment, but it will not protect the crusher itself.

Does burden depth matter more than belt width?

Both matter, but burden depth is often the overlooked parameter. Belt width tells the supplier how much lateral coverage is needed. Burden depth tells the supplier how far the magnet must reach into the material stream. A wide belt with shallow burden may be easier than a narrower belt carrying a deep bed of dense ore or wet aggregate.

Is a permanent or electromagnetic separator better for high suspension height?

The better option depends on the working distance and duty. Permanent separators can suit many conveyor applications when the height and burden depth are within the selected range. Electromagnetic separators may be reviewed for higher suspension heights, deeper burden or adjustable magnetic field requirements. The decision should be based on measured conveyor data, not the product name alone.

What photos should be sent with a quotation request?

Send photos of the proposed installation point from both sides of the conveyor, the upstream and downstream transfer areas, the support structure, material burden on the belt and the available discharge side. Include a simple marked photo or sketch showing the measured height from the belt and from the top of burden to the planned magnet face.

Conclusion

Suspension height is one of the most important factors in conveyor magnetic separator performance. If the magnet is installed too high, the magnetic field may not reach the tramp iron effectively, especially when material burden is deep, wet or fast-moving. The correct choice depends on the full conveyor condition, not only the belt width.

A magnetic separator for a coal conveyor removes ferrous tramp metal from coal before it reaches crushers, screens, transfer chutes, feeders or downstream process equipment. For African coal handling plants, the right separator is selected by conveyor and material conditions: belt width, belt speed, burden depth, moisture, installation height, tramp iron size and cleaning method.

This article is for coal mine operators, power plant fuel handling teams, cement plants using coal, bulk terminal engineers and project buyers in South Africa and other African markets. It explains when to use an overband magnetic separator, when a suspended permanent magnet may be enough, and when an electromagnetic separator should be reviewed.

Key Takeaways

  • Coal conveyor separator selection must start with belt width, burden depth, belt speed and installation height.
  • Self-cleaning overband magnets are commonly reviewed for continuous coal handling where tramp iron appears regularly.
  • Permanent magnets can suit many standard duties; electromagnetic separators may be reviewed for deeper burden or adjustable force needs.
  • Moisture, dust, coal lump size and transfer-point layout affect real performance.
  • Magnetic separators remove ferrous metal; non-ferrous detection requires different equipment.
  • A quote should be based on operating data, not only a conveyor photo or equipment name.

Use Case: Tramp Iron Removal on Coal Conveyors

Coal conveyors can carry tramp iron from mining tools, crusher liners, bolts, screen parts, rail fragments, loader bucket teeth, conveyor hardware and maintenance debris. If this metal reaches a crusher or transfer chute, it can damage equipment, cut belts, block chutes or force shutdowns.

In South African coalfields, regional power generation, cement fuel preparation and port handling operations, coal conveyors often operate in dusty environments with high throughput and limited maintenance windows. A properly selected magnetic separator creates a controlled removal point before the tramp iron reaches more vulnerable equipment.

The separator is not only a contamination device. It is part of plant protection. Its job is to remove ferrous metal at a predictable location where maintenance teams can inspect, collect and dispose of the captured material safely.

Recommended Equipment Types

The most common choice for frequent tramp iron removal is a self-cleaning overband magnetic separator. It is installed above the belt and uses a discharge belt to carry captured metal out of the magnetic zone. This is useful when the coal conveyor runs continuously or when manual cleaning would interrupt production.

A suspended permanent magnetic separator can be suitable where tramp iron is occasional and the plant can safely clean the magnet during planned stops. It can be simple and effective when the magnet can be installed close enough to the coal burden and when the burden depth is not excessive.

A suspended electromagnetic conveyor belt separator may be reviewed when the coal burden is deeper, installation height is higher, or adjustable magnetic force is required. It needs electrical power and control equipment, so the site must consider power reliability, maintenance access and operating procedures.

Key Selection Parameters

Belt width is the first basic parameter. The separator must cover the actual coal stream, not only the nominal conveyor size. If coal is loaded off-centre, the magnet position or magnetic face coverage must be reviewed.

Burden depth is often more important than buyers expect. A shallow coal layer allows easier magnetic reach. A deep coal bed can hide tramp iron below the surface, especially when fine coal fills the gaps around larger pieces. The supplier needs burden depth at the installation point, not only average capacity.

Belt speed affects the available capture time. A faster belt gives the magnet less time to lift ferrous metal from the burden. Capacity per hour, coal lump size, moisture, dust, installation angle and the expected size of tramp iron all affect the recommended separator type.

Permanent vs Electromagnetic Coal Conveyor Separators

A permanent separator uses permanent magnet material and does not need electrical power to generate the magnetic field. For many coal conveyor applications, this can be practical and reliable. A self-cleaning permanent overband unit still needs a motor for the cleaning belt, but not for the magnetic field.

An electromagnetic separator uses an energized coil. It may be appropriate when the conveyor has deeper burden, higher suspension height or a requirement for adjustable magnetic intensity. The trade-off is more electrical dependency and additional maintenance considerations.

The correct decision should be based on the coal handling duty. Permanent is not automatically too weak, and electromagnetic is not automatically the best choice. The application data decides.

Self-Cleaning vs Manual-Cleaning

Self-cleaning is usually preferred where tramp iron appears every shift or where the conveyor cannot be stopped frequently. The separator continuously discharges captured metal to one side of the conveyor, reducing manual intervention and helping the plant maintain throughput.

Manual-cleaning suspended magnets may suit low-contamination or smaller conveyor applications. They require safe isolation and cleaning procedures. If the magnet captures metal often, manual cleaning can become a safety and downtime issue.

Common Mistakes in Coal Conveyor Applications

One common mistake is selecting a magnet by belt width alone. Two coal conveyors with the same width may have different burden depth, belt speed, moisture and installation height. These differences can change the separator recommendation.

Another mistake is installing the separator too high. The air gap between the magnet and the top of the coal burden reduces magnetic reach. The structure should allow the magnet to be close enough for capture while preserving safe clearance for coal flow and large lumps.

A third mistake is failing to plan the discharge side. Captured tramp iron needs a chute, bin or safe collection area. If discharge is blocked by structure, walkways or other equipment, the plant may create a new maintenance problem.

Installation and Maintenance Notes

The separator is typically installed before crushers, screens, transfer points or process equipment that needs protection. Cross-belt installation is common when metal must be discharged to one side. Inline installation can be reviewed where the layout supports discharge in the conveyor direction.

Maintenance teams should inspect the cleaning belt, motor, bearings, guards, suspension frame, discharge chute and captured metal bin. For electromagnetic separators, control panels, cable routing and cooling requirements should also be checked. Coal dust, outdoor exposure and high ambient temperature should be discussed before final selection.

When This Product Is Suitable

A coal conveyor magnetic separator is suitable when ferrous tramp iron may enter the coal stream and damage equipment or interrupt production. It is relevant for coal mines, coal washing plants, power plant fuel conveyors, cement plants, ports and bulk terminals.

It is especially useful where the plant wants a visible protection point before critical equipment. The separator can help maintenance teams identify recurring tramp iron sources and improve housekeeping around conveyors and transfer points.

When This Product Is Not Suitable

A conveyor magnetic separator is not suitable for removing most non-ferrous metals such as aluminium, copper or brass. If the risk includes non-ferrous contamination, the plant should review metal detection or eddy current separation separately.

It may also be unsuitable as a standalone solution if the coal burden is too deep, the magnet must be mounted too high, or the conveyor layout prevents safe metal discharge. In such cases, the plant may need to improve loading, reduce burden depth, change the installation point or combine technologies.

Information Needed Before Quotation

Before requesting a quotation, provide actual operating data from the conveyor. This prevents undersizing and avoids a recommendation based only on generic assumptions. Photos and drawings are useful, but they do not replace belt width, burden depth and installation height data.

FAQ

What magnetic separator is used on a coal conveyor?

Coal conveyors commonly use overband magnetic separators, suspended permanent magnets or suspended electromagnetic separators to remove ferrous tramp metal from the belt. The correct type depends on belt width, belt speed, burden depth, installation height, frequency of tramp iron and cleaning method. Self-cleaning overband magnets are often reviewed where coal handling lines run continuously.

Why is tramp iron removal important in coal handling?

Tramp iron can damage crushers, screens, feeders, chutes and conveyor belts. In African coal handling operations, unplanned downtime can be costly because sites may run long conveyors, dusty transfer points and limited maintenance windows. Magnetic separation helps remove ferrous steel pieces before they reach vulnerable equipment.

Is a permanent magnet enough for coal conveyors?

A permanent magnet can be enough for many coal conveyor duties when the burden depth, suspension height and tramp iron size are within the selected model range. If the burden is deep, the installation point is high, or the plant needs adjustable magnetic force, an electromagnetic separator may need to be reviewed.

Where should the separator be installed?

The separator is usually installed before the crusher, screen, transfer chute or process equipment that needs protection. It should be positioned where the coal burden is stable and where captured metal can be discharged safely. The support structure, guarding and maintenance access should be reviewed before finalizing the layout.

Can magnetic separators remove non-ferrous metals from coal?

No. Standard conveyor magnets remove ferrous magnetic metals such as iron and many steels. They do not remove most aluminium, copper, brass or weakly magnetic stainless steel. If non-ferrous metal detection or recovery is required, the plant should separately review metal detectors or eddy current separation.

title: Conveyor Belt Magnetic Separators for South African Mines
excerpt: Learn how South African mines choose conveyor belt magnetic separators for tramp iron removal, crusher protection, belt width and burden depth.
summary: Selection guide for South African mining buyers comparing overband, suspended permanent and electromagnetic conveyor belt magnetic separators.
content:
SEO Meta

  • SEO Title: Conveyor Belt Magnetic Separators for South African Mines
  • Meta Description: Learn how South African mines choose conveyor belt magnetic separators for tramp iron removal, crusher protection, belt width and burden depth.
  • URL Slug: conveyor-belt-magnetic-separators-south-african-mines
  • Primary Keyword: conveyor belt magnetic separator South Africa
  • Secondary Keywords: magnetic separator South Africa, overband magnetic separator, suspended magnetic separator, tramp metal removal, magnetic separator for mining
  • Search Intent: Commercial investigation and equipment selection
  • Target Country or Region: South Africa and nearby African mining markets
  • Target Buyer: Mine engineers, plant managers, maintenance teams, EPC contractors and procurement teams
  • Suggested CTA: Send conveyor and material data to Cowin Magnet for selection advice and quotation.

A conveyor belt magnetic separator is used above or near a conveyor to remove ferrous tramp metal before it damages crushers, screens, transfer chutes, mills or downstream process equipment. For South African mines, the main buying question is not simply which magnet is strongest. The real question is which separator can reach the tramp iron through the actual material burden, fit the conveyor layout, discharge metal safely and operate reliably in the mine environment.

This guide is written for mining plants, quarry operators, coal handling sites, cement raw material lines and mineral processing projects in South Africa and wider African markets. It explains how to choose between overband, suspended permanent and suspended electromagnetic conveyor belt magnetic separators, what data to prepare before quotation, and which mistakes commonly lead to poor separation results.

Key Takeaways

  • Selection depends on belt width, burden depth, suspension height, belt speed, material type and tramp iron size.
  • Self-cleaning overband magnets are usually preferred where tramp metal appears frequently or conveyor uptime is critical.
  • Permanent magnets suit many standard conveyor protection duties; electromagnetic separators may be reviewed for deeper burden or adjustable force requirements.
  • Installation position and discharge path are as important as magnetic strength.
  • A proper quote should be based on operating data, not only a photo or belt width.
  • Magnetic separators remove ferrous metal; non-ferrous detection or recovery may need other equipment.

Use Case: Conveyor Protection in South African Mines

South African mining sites often handle abrasive material, long conveyors, variable feed rates and large lumps from primary crushing or ROM stockpiles. Ferrous tramp metal can come from bucket teeth, drill rods, liner fragments, bolts, screen parts, tools, wire rope and conveyor hardware. If these pieces reach a crusher or screen, they can cause belt damage, blocked chutes, broken liners, emergency shutdowns and unplanned maintenance.

A conveyor belt magnetic separator is installed to remove magnetic ferrous metal from the conveyed material stream. In practical terms, it acts as a protection device for mechanical equipment and a contamination-control device for the process. It can be used before jaw crushers, cone crushers, impact crushers, secondary crushers, screens, transfer stations, coal handling conveyors, aggregate lines and recycling feed belts.

Recommended Equipment Types

The most common choice for continuous conveyor tramp iron removal is an overband magnetic separator. It is suspended over the belt and usually includes a self-cleaning discharge belt that carries captured metal away from the main material flow. This makes it suitable for mines where stopping the conveyor for cleaning is not practical.

A suspended permanent magnetic separator may be suitable where the contamination level is low and manual cleaning is acceptable. It can be simple and effective when the burden depth is manageable and the magnet can be installed close enough to the material. A suspended electromagnetic conveyor belt separator may be considered when the plant needs adjustable magnetic force or when the burden depth and suspension height require a stronger field review.

For some sites, a magnetic head pulley or drum magnet may also be reviewed at discharge points. These are not direct substitutes for every overband magnet application, but they can be useful where the conveyor layout and material trajectory allow separation at the pulley or transfer point.

Key Selection Parameters

The first parameter is belt width. The magnetic field must cover the actual material stream, including off-centre loading if the conveyor is not evenly loaded. A separator selected only from nominal belt width may miss material concentrated on one side of the belt.

The second parameter is burden depth, which is the thickness of material on the conveyor. A shallow burden is easier for the magnet to penetrate. A deep burden can hide tramp iron under a layer of ore, coal or aggregate. This is one of the most common reasons a magnet that looks large enough on paper performs poorly at site.

The third parameter is suspension height. Magnetic force drops as the distance from the magnet face increases. The separator should be installed with enough clearance for safe material flow but close enough to attract tramp iron. Other important parameters include belt speed, capacity per hour, material lump size, moisture level, material density, installation angle, power availability and expected tramp iron size.

Permanent vs Electromagnetic Separators

A permanent magnetic separator uses permanent magnet material and does not need electrical power to create the magnetic field. For many South African conveyor protection applications, this can be practical because the magnetic field is always available and the system is relatively simple. A self-cleaning permanent overband magnet still needs a motor for the cleaning belt, but not for the magnetic field itself.

An electromagnetic separator uses an energized coil. It may be reviewed when the application needs higher magnetic reach, adjustable operating conditions or site-specific control. The trade-off is that it requires reliable power, controls and maintenance attention. It should not be chosen only because it sounds more powerful. The right choice depends on the burden depth, suspension height, duty cycle and site conditions.

Self-Cleaning vs Manual-Cleaning

A self-cleaning separator is usually preferred where tramp metal appears regularly. The continuous cleaning belt removes captured metal from the magnetic zone and discharges it to the side of the conveyor. This helps keep the conveyor running and reduces the need for operators to stop the line for manual cleaning.

A manual-cleaning suspended magnet can still be suitable for lighter-duty or occasional-contamination applications. It may fit smaller conveyors, temporary installations or sites where inspection and cleaning are easy to schedule. The decision should consider safety procedures, production pressure, the frequency of tramp iron and the physical access around the conveyor.

Common Selection Mistakes

One mistake is selecting only by belt width. Belt width is necessary, but it does not describe material depth, lump size, feed rate or magnet height. Two conveyors with the same width can require different separator sizes.

Another mistake is ignoring the discharge side. Removed metal must be dropped into a safe collection zone. If there is no space for discharge, the installation may create a maintenance hazard or cause metal to fall back into the material stream.

A third mistake is assuming the magnet will remove all metal. Magnetic separators remove ferrous magnetic material. They do not solve non-ferrous contamination, stainless steel detection or every process quality issue. If the risk includes non-ferrous metal, the plant should review metal detectors or eddy current separators separately.

Installation and Maintenance Notes

Installation should consider structural support, vibration, conveyor guarding, access platforms, lifting clearance, chute design and collection bins. The magnet should be positioned where the material is stable enough for separation and before the equipment that needs protection.

Routine maintenance should include checking the self-cleaning belt, bearings, motor, guards, suspension frame, discharge area and collected metal bin. For electromagnetic models, electrical controls and cooling arrangements should also be inspected. In dusty, wet, coastal or high-temperature environments, protection level and corrosion resistance should be discussed before final selection.

When This Product Is Suitable

A conveyor belt magnetic separator is suitable when ferrous tramp metal may be mixed with ore, coal, aggregate, limestone, recycled material or other conveyed bulk solids. It is particularly relevant before crushers, screens, transfer stations and process equipment that would be expensive to repair after metal impact.

It is also suitable when the buyer wants a continuous, visible protection point that can be inspected by maintenance teams. Mines, quarries, cement plants, coal handling systems and recycling plants can all use this type of equipment when the material stream and installation conditions are appropriate.

When This Product Is Not Suitable

This product is not suitable as the only solution for non-ferrous metal removal. Aluminium, copper and brass require different separation or detection methods. It may also be unsuitable if the burden depth is too high, the magnet must be mounted too far from the material, or the conveyor layout prevents safe discharge of captured metal.

If the plant cannot confirm source publication data, operating conditions or material characteristics, equipment selection should remain preliminary. A responsible supplier should request operating data before making a firm recommendation.

Information Needed Before Quotation

Before requesting a quote, send clear operating data. This allows Cowin Magnet to recommend whether a permanent overband magnet, suspended permanent magnet, electromagnetic separator or another configuration should be reviewed. It also reduces the risk of undersizing or overcomplicating the solution.

Quotation Checklist

  • Material type
  • Particle size
  • Moisture level
  • Capacity per hour
  • Conveyor belt width
  • Belt speed
  • Burden depth
  • Installation height
  • Tramp iron size
  • Cleaning method
  • Power availability
  • Working environment

FAQ

What is a conveyor belt magnetic separator used for in a mine?

It is used to remove ferrous tramp metal from material moving on a conveyor before it reaches crushers, screens, mills or other process equipment. In South African mining conditions, it is commonly considered for coal, iron ore, manganese, chrome, gold, quarry stone and aggregate conveyors where steel fragments can damage equipment or cause unplanned shutdowns.

Should a South African mine choose a permanent or electromagnetic separator?

A permanent separator is often suitable for standard tramp iron removal where the burden depth and installation height are within the magnetic reach of the selected model. An electromagnetic separator may be reviewed when the burden is deeper, the suspension height is higher, or adjustable magnetic force is required. The correct choice depends on site data rather than the country or industry alone.

Where should the separator be installed on the conveyor?

The usual location is before the crusher, screen or transfer point that needs protection. It may be installed cross-belt or inline depending on the conveyor layout and discharge path. The installation should allow safe clearance above the material, enough space for removed metal to discharge, and practical maintenance access around the magnet and support frame.

Can a conveyor belt magnet remove all metal contamination?

No. A conveyor belt magnetic separator removes ferrous magnetic metal. It will not remove most aluminium, copper, brass or weakly magnetic stainless steel. If the plant also needs non-ferrous metal recovery or detection, eddy current separation or metal detection may need to be reviewed as a separate part of the process.

What information is needed before requesting a quote?

Send material type, particle size, moisture, capacity per hour, belt width, belt speed, burden depth, installation height, tramp iron size, preferred cleaning method, power availability and working environment. Photos or drawings of the conveyor are also useful. Without this data, a supplier can only provide a rough recommendation.

Is a self-cleaning separator necessary?

Self-cleaning is recommended when tramp iron appears frequently, when the conveyor runs for long shifts, or when stopping the belt for manual cleaning would reduce production. Manual-cleaning suspended magnets can be suitable when contamination is rare and site procedures allow safe cleaning. The decision should consider uptime, safety and maintenance access.

Conclusion

Choosing a conveyor belt magnetic separator for South African mines requires more than matching a catalog model to belt width. The correct recommendation depends on the material, burden depth, belt speed, installation height, tramp iron risk, cleaning method and site environment.
